Context & Goal:
Please develop a comprehensive, enterprise-grade Aviation Fuel Management System. The application must adhere to modern international airport standards (including JIG compliance for quality checks) and be optimized for both desktop and offline-capable mobile/tablet use on the apron.

Critically, the system must utilize a strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) mechanism. Staff from different units must only have access to the modules, views, and data strictly relevant to their operational duties. Do not include any features related to Finance, Billing, Invoicing, Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), or Customs Duty.

Please design the system architecture, database schema, and core UI/UX flows based on the following detailed requirements:

1. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) & Governance
The system must enforce data ownership boundaries. The Fuel Services Section owns the operational data.

System Administrator (IT Dept): Full backend access for system maintenance, user provisioning, and server management. No rights to alter day-to-day operational data.

Fuel Services Manager / Duty Manager: Full read/write access to dashboards, reports, and operational records. Can allocate refuelers and assign operators to flights.

Into-Plane (ITP) Operator: Mobile/tablet access only. Restricted to inputting flight refueling data, quality control (QC) checks, and viewing their specific job assignments. Cannot edit past records after submission.

Depot Operator: Restricted to inputting data for bulk tanker discharges, refueler loading (bridging), facility transfers, and static tank inventory readings.

Executive Management: Read-only access to a dedicated Executive Dashboard featuring daily stock summaries, variance vs. last year, month-to-date performance, and forecasting.

Commercial Division: Read-only access restricted strictly to aggregate sales volumes, peak-hour comparisons, and route-based performance metrics. No access to technical stock levels or internal operational remarks.

2. Core Operational Modules (Data Input)
Flight Refueling (Into-Plane Operations):

Digital forms for domestic and commercial flight refueling.

Metering Reconciliation: Mandatory entry of totalizer data (Opening Reading, Closing Reading, Total Volume) for every meter run (aircraft refueling, defueling, QC checks).

Granular Timestamps: Must log Arrived, Commenced, Completed, Position Time (vehicle at aircraft), Initial End, Final Start/End (for top-ups), and Clearance (vehicle leaves safety zone).

Refueler Loading (Bridging/Transfer): Track fuel transferred from New/Old Fuel Farms to refuelers, including Visual and CWD quality control checks.

Tanker & Barge Discharge: Interfaces to record bulk Diesel and Petrol receipts from marine vessels. Must include Bill of Lading quantities, specific gravity, and temperature readings with automated validation against vessel calibration charts.

Vehicle & Seaplane Fueling: Modules to log gasoline/diesel refueling for Ground Support Equipment at Airside/Landside Fuel Stations (AFS/LFS), and dedicated seaplane operations.

Depot Stock Inventory: Daily entry of static tank levels (Jet A-1, Diesel, Petrol) for reconciliation.

3. Advanced Jet A-1 Forecasting & Scenario Planning
Real-Time Variance: Maintain a continuous timeline. Once a flight is refueled, replace the forecasted uplift volume with the actual logged volume in real-time. Immediately apply the variance to the remaining stock to adjust the "Stock Will Last Till" date.

Three-Scenario Modeling: Toggle between Nominal (baseline), Upper (high-consumption), and Lower (low-consumption) demand scenarios. Must account for Tank Ullage to warn if incoming shipments exceed physical capacity.

Historical Overlay: Visually compare current stock depletion curves directly against the same period from previous years.

4. Dashboards & Analytics
Live Dashboard Widgets:

Capacity Gauges: Donut/liquid fill charts showing current fuel vs. maximum capacity.

Pending Operations: Active refueling or tanker discharges currently in progress with running timers.

Heat Maps & Scatter Graphs: Visualizing fuel uplift volumes to identify peak times, and scatter plots of Volume vs. Duration.

Critical Alerts: Automated warnings for tanks falling below safety stock levels.

Reporting (Exportable to PDF/CSV):

Stock Availability & Fuel Forecasts (predicting critical levels up to 1 month out based on 5-year historical data).

Granular Sales & Commercial Analysis segmented by Aircraft Operator, Aircraft Type, and Route (capable of integrating with SITA AMS).

Peak Utilization Analysis comparing peak days/hours year-over-year.

5. Non-Functional Requirements
Offline Mode (Crucial): If operators are in remote apron areas with poor Wi-Fi/4G connectivity, the mobile progressive web app (PWA) or native app must cache data locally and auto-sync when connection is restored.

Audit Trail: Every create, edit, and delete action must be strictly timestamped with the User ID for complete accountability.

UI/UX: Must feature large, high-contrast touch targets for apron workers wearing PPE, and apply standard data entry validation to minimize human error.

**Defining the Objective**

I'm currently focused on defining the core objective: a high-fidelity, enterprise-grade Aviation Fuel Management System. This involves deep diving into the specific needs and functionalities required, ensuring I fully grasp the project's scope.


**Outlining Core Features**

I'm now outlining the core features and tech stack. This involves deciding on specific React libraries: React 18+, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React, and Recharts, with D3 as a potential backup. I'm structuring this around Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), with modules for Flight Refueling, Refueler Loading, Tanker Discharge, Stock Inventory, and Forecasting. I'm also planning dashboards with live widgets, capacity gauges, heatmaps, and alerts.


**Refining UX Details**

I'm now zeroing in on crucial UX refinements, ensuring offline functionality with a clear indicator and implementing a robust audit trail. High-contrast options and touch-friendly controls are also top priorities to enhance usability for all operators. I've been organizing the components directory structure as well. I'm focusing on metadata, types, and constants. I'm defining a Role enum and a FlightLog interface.


**Developing Mock Data**

I'm now generating realistic mock data, including user roles, tank data for Jet A-1 and Diesel, and flight schedules. I'm focusing on ensuring it's representative of operational scenarios to aid in testing and visualization.
I've started building the layout components, incorporating a sidebar for navigation based on user roles and a top bar with a user profile and offline mode indicator. I'm using Tailwind for responsive design, particularly with a mobile-first approach to better assist operators.
I've started to work on the executive and operational dashboard components. I plan to use Recharts for stock levels, trends, and peak times. I plan to implement an alerts section.
I'm now focusing on a critical into-plane form, designed with large buttons and easy-to-use inputs such as meter open and close, along with automatic volume calculation. I'm including timestamps for positioning, start, end, and clearance.


**Implementing Forecasting**

I'm currently focused on the forecasting module, specifically building scenario toggles for nominal, upper, and lower stock depletion forecasts. I'm visualizing these scenarios in a chart that displays stock levels over time, compared to a set threshold.



**Drafting the React Logic**

I'm now drafting the React logic, starting with layout components using a fixed sidebar and Lucide React icons. Recharts will handle robust charting, and I'm designing forms as controlled components. The IntoPlaneForm needs detailed fields per specifications, like "Meter Open," "Meter Close," and "Position Time." I'll also use `navigator.onLine` for offline mode simulation.

Context & Goal:
Please architect and develop a comprehensive, enterprise-grade Aviation Fuel Management System. The application must adhere to modern international airport standards (including JIG compliance for fuel quality) and be optimized for both desktop and offline-capable mobile/tablet use on the apron.

The system will digitize operations across New Fuel Farms (NFF), Old Fuel Farms (OFF), Airside/Landside Fuel Stations (AFS/LFS), and Into-Plane (ITP) Apron/Seaplane operations. Do not include any features related to Finance, Billing, Invoicing, Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), or Customs Duty at this stage.

Please design the system architecture, database schema, and core UI/UX flows based on the following exhaustive requirements:

1. System Governance & Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
The system must enforce strict data ownership boundaries. The Fuel Services Section retains exclusive authority over operational records. No external department can alter the primary operational dataset.

System Administrator (IT Dept): Full backend access for system maintenance, server management, and security. No intervention in day-to-day operational data entry.

Fuel Services Executive / Duty Manager: Full read/write access to dashboards, reports, and settings. Capable of allocating refuelers, assigning operators to flights, and modifying schedules.

ITP Operator (Apron): Input access only. Can view assigned jobs, enter flight refueling data, and log QC checks. Cannot edit records once submitted.

Depot Operator: Input access only. Responsible for logging tanker discharges, refueler loading (bridging), facility transfers, and daily static tank dips.

Executive Management: Access restricted to a dedicated Executive Dashboard module containing static daily stock summaries, month-to-date performance, and variance reporting.

Commercial & Finance Divisions: Read-only access restricted strictly to aggregate sales volumes, peak-hour comparisons, and route-based performance metrics. No access to technical stock levels or internal operational remarks.

2. Functional Requirements: Data Input Modules
2.1 Flight Refueling (Into-Plane Operations):

Integration with the Airport Operational Control Centre (AOCC) to pull pre-refueling flight details.

Metering Reconciliation: Mandatory entry of totalizer data (Opening Reading, Closing Reading, Total Net Volume) for all meter runs (aircraft, QC checks, inter-farm transfers).

Granular Timestamps: Must precisely log: Arrived, Commenced, Position Time (vehicle at aircraft), Initial End, Final Start (for airline-requested top-ups), Final End, and Clearance (vehicle clears the safety zone), along with standard "Completed" time.

2.2 Refueler Loading (Bridging) & QC: Track fuel transferred from storage tanks to refuelers, capture mobile vehicle status, and mandate inputs for Visual and CWD Quality Control checks.

2.3 Tanker & Barge Discharge:

Distinct input modes for marine Tankers vs. Barges.

Data entry for Bill of Lading (B/L) quantities, specific gravity, and temperature.

Validation Engine: Ensure entered volumes automatically validate against vessel calibration charts.

Strict Segregation: Enforce data separation for Diesel and Petrol receipts to ensure inventory accuracy.

2.4 Ground & Seaplane Operations: Modules to record gasoline/diesel refueling for Ground Support Equipment (AFS/LFS) and dedicated logging for seaplane operations.

2.5 Depot Fuel Inventory: Daily data entry interface for static tank levels (Jet A-1, Diesel, Petrol) to support reconciliation.

3. Advanced Jet A-1 Forecasting & Scenario Planning
Real-Time Forecast-to-Actual Conversion: Maintain a rolling timeline. Upon successful logging of a refueling transaction, the system must immediately replace the forecasted uplift with the actual delivered volume.

Live Variance Application: Calculate the variance between forecasted vs. actual uplift and instantly apply it to the remaining stock projection to adjust the "Stock Will Last Till" date.

Three-Scenario Modeling: Users must be able to toggle between Nominal (baseline schedule), Upper (high-consumption), and Lower (low-consumption) scenarios. All scenarios must calculate Tank Ullage to warn if scheduled shipments exceed available storage capacity.

Schedule & Shipment Modification: Authorized users can flag flights as "Cancelled," insert "Ad-hoc" flights, and alter expected shipment arrival dates/quantities to simulate supply chain delays.

Comparative Historical Analysis: A visual overlay allowing users to compare the current stock depletion curve directly against data from the exact same period in previous years.

4. Dashboards & Analytics
Central Operational Dashboard Widgets:

Capacity Gauges: Donut/liquid fill charts showing current fuel vs. maximum capacity (Jet-A1, Diesel, Petrol).

Pending Operations: Active refueling and tanker discharges currently in progress with live running timers.

Heat Maps & Scatter Graphs: A grid showing fuel uplift volume to identify peak times/carriers, and a scatter plot analyzing Volume vs. Duration.

Trend Graphs & Bar Charts: Current month vs. previous month sales, and equipment/vehicle usage charts.

Critical Alerts: Automated warnings for tanks dropping below safety stock levels.

Executive View Dashboard:

Static Daily Stock Summary: Opening Stock, Physical Balance, Usable Fuel (Balance minus Dead Stock).

Threshold Indicator: Visual status based on a strictly defined 22-Day Stock Coverage Threshold.

Shipment Window Analysis: Next Arrival Date, Order Quantity, and "Stock Balance to Shipment Arrival Window" (in days).

Month-to-Date (MTD) Performance: Total volume, flights served, and % variance vs. last year.

Reporting (Exportable to PDF/CSV):

Predictive Stock Availability generated using a 5-year historical data analysis of the same period.

Granular Commercial Reports segmented by Aircraft Operator, Aircraft Type, and Route (Note: system must be capable of integration with SITA AMS to pull Route data for profitability analysis).

Peak Utilization Analysis comparing peak day/hour volumes year-over-year.

5. Non-Functional Requirements
Offline Mode (Critical): The mobile application (PWA or Native) must cache data locally when operating in remote apron areas with poor connectivity, automatically syncing when the connection is restored.

Audit Trail: Every create, edit, and delete action must be strictly time-stamped with the User ID.

Data Validation: Apply strict input validations across all forms to minimize human error on the tarmac.

I'll provide you with both the Database Schema architecture and the Mobile UI/UX Wireframe concepts.

This combination will give your development team a complete technical blueprint to start building the backend logic and the frontend interfaces simultaneously.

Part 1: Core Database Schema (Entity-Relationship Design)
To support the robust reporting, real-time forecasting, and granular timestamping required by international standards, your database needs a highly normalized relational structure.

Here are the critical tables and relationships to instruct your database engineers to build:

1. Governance & Access Control


Users Table: UserID (PK), Username, PasswordHash, RoleID (FK), Status (Active/Inactive).
+3


Roles Table: RoleID (PK), RoleName (e.g., Admin, Duty Manager, ITP Operator, Depot Operator, Executive, Commercial) .
+3


Audit_Logs Table: LogID (PK), UserID (FK), ActionType (Create, Edit, Delete), AffectedTable, Timestamp, OfflineSyncFlag (Boolean).
+2

2. Assets & Inventory Master Data


Storage_Facilities Table: FacilityID (PK), FacilityName (NFF, OFF, AFS, LFS, Seaplane Base).
+2


Storage_Tanks Table: TankID (PK), FacilityID (FK), ProductType (Jet A-1, Diesel, Petrol), MaxCapacity, DeadStock, SafeStockLevel.
+4


Mobile_Equipment Table: VehicleID (PK), EquipmentType (Refueler, Dispenser, GSE), RegistrationNo, CurrentStatus (Active, Maintenance), CurrentVolume.
+4

3. Flight & Schedule Management


Flight_Schedules Table: FlightID (PK), FlightNumber, OperatorID (FK - Airline), AircraftType, Route (Origin/Destination), ScheduledTime, Forecasted_Uplift_Volume, Status (Scheduled, Cancelled, Ad-hoc, Completed) .
+3

4. Operational Transactions (The Core Engines)


ITP_Refueling_Logs Table: LogID (PK), FlightID (FK), OperatorID (FK), VehicleID (FK).


Meters: Totalizer_Opening, Totalizer_Closing, Net_Volume_Delivered.
+3


Timestamps: Time_Arrived, Time_Positioned, Time_Commenced, Time_Initial_End, Time_Final_Start, Time_Final_End, Time_Cleared, Time_Completed .
+3


Marine_Discharge_Receipts Table: ReceiptID (PK), VesselType (Tanker, Barge), ProductType, Bill_Of_Lading_Qty, SpecificGravity, Temperature, NetReceivedVolume, TargetFacilityID (FK) .
+4


Quality_Control_Checks Table: QcID (PK), ReferenceLogID (FK - links to ITP or Bridging log), CheckType (Visual, CWD, SWD), Appearance_ClearBright (Boolean), WaterSedimentsFound (Boolean), FlowrateLPM .
+4

Part 2: UI/UX Wireframe Concepts for ITP Operators (Mobile/Tablet)
Because ITP Operators wear heavy PPE and work on the apron under glaring sunlight, the UI must be high-contrast, utilize oversized tap targets, and operate seamlessly in "Offline Mode".

Here is the flow to provide to your UI/UX designer:


Global App Header: Always displays the logged-in Operator Name, the currently assigned Vehicle ID, and a dynamic Sync Status Icon (Green = Online/Synced; Orange = Offline/Saving Locally).

Screen 1: The Duty Dashboard (Task Hub)

Displays a vertically scrolling list of "Assigned Flights" pulled directly from the AOCC.

Each flight card shows: Flight No, Aircraft Reg, Bay/Stand Number, and an oversized "START JOB" button.

Screen 2: Ramp Arrival & Timestamps

Upon tapping "START JOB," the user enters the active flow.

Massive, one-tap stopwatch buttons for granular timestamping: [Log Position Time] followed by [Log Commence Time] .

Screen 3: Metering & Volume (The most critical screen)

Numerical keypad interface for entering the Opening Totalizer reading.
+1

Upon fueling completion, operator taps [Initial End].

Operator enters Closing Totalizer. The app automatically calculates the Net Volume.


Optional toggle: "+ Add Top-Up" which reveals Final Start and Final End timestamps if the airline requests more fuel.

Screen 4: Quality Control & Sign-off

Simple, oversized toggle switches (Yes/No) for mandatory JIG checks: "Panel Closed?", "Walk Around Done?", "Appearance Clear & Bright?", "Water/Sediments Free?" .

Tap [Clearance] (vehicle leaves aircraft).

Final digital sign-off and submit. If offline, it saves to local cache and syncs when back in the office.

**Defining Project Scope**

Okay, I'm focusing on defining the scope for this expansion project. Right now, I'm honing in on the key requirement: a System Admin Module. That's the starting point, and I'm assessing the implications of that module to determine where it fits into the current system and what foundational changes may be necessary to accommodate it.


**Expanding Module Functionality**

I'm now diving into the user management specifics within the System Admin Module, focusing on user/role management. I've progressed to consider a Commercial Reports Module, planning sales and carrier analytics reporting. I'm prioritizing user experience with role-based dashboard view toggles, specifically for system admins and executives, thinking of a state to manage this. I also need to address UI issues in the "Add Flight" modal to improve readability. Finally, there's a need for a Seaplane Entry Module.


**Outlining New Modules**

I've outlined three new components: SystemAdmin, CommercialReports, and Seaplane. I'm focusing on their data mockups and required elements like user tables, charts, and input forms. I'm also preparing to integrate user role checks and view toggles into the Dashboard, and to apply Tailwind classes to the schedule inputs.


**Updating Component Integration**

I'm now integrating the new modules by modifying `App.tsx` to import and render `SystemAdmin`, `CommercialReports`, and `Seaplane`. I'm also updating `Sidebar.tsx` to include new menu items accessible by role: 'admin', 'reports', and 'seaplane'. I'm also currently extracting the dashboard layouts into sub-render functions to enable view toggling based on the user's role. I will add a `viewMode` state.


**Refining UI Elements**

I'm addressing the "flight fields are dark" issue; I'll ensure inputs use `bg-white`, `text-slate-900`, and `border-gray-300` for better visibility. The Seaplane Module is taking shape, and will be structured similar to `IntoPlane.tsx` or `Bridging.tsx`, with adjustments for seaplane specifics, such as dock location. I'm focusing on the component structure, and preparing the content for SystemAdmin, CommercialReports, and Seaplane, and am now working to address file updates.


**Prioritizing Module Changes**

I'm now prioritizing the System Admin and Commercial Reports modules, as well as the dashboard view toggles for admins and executives, per the prompt. I've broken down tasks: updating `App.tsx` imports, adjusting `Sidebar.tsx` menu lists, adding toggle logic to `Dashboard.tsx`, and fixing input styles in `Schedule.tsx`. Finally, I'll create the component files `SystemAdmin.tsx`, `CommercialReports.tsx`, and `Seaplane.tsx`, focusing on the content for each component next.


**Developing Module Layouts**

I've begun building the layouts for the new modules, creating `SystemAdmin.tsx`, `CommercialReports.tsx`, and `Seaplane.tsx`. I'm starting by adding the basic structure and placeholder content for each, including icons and import statements. I'm focusing on user table and chart rendering, and basic design implementation.

To address your request, I will implement the System Admin and Commercial Reports modules, create the Seaplane operations view, enable dashboard toggling for Executives/Admins, and fix the readability issues in the Schedule modal.

### Changes Breakdown

1.  **`components/SystemAdmin.tsx`**: A new module for user provisioning, system health monitoring, and security audit logs.
2.  **`components/CommercialReports.tsx`**: A new analytics module featuring sales performance by airline, route profitability, and revenue trends using charts.
3.  **`components/Seaplane.tsx`**: A specialized data entry form for seaplane refueling at docks (Terminal A/B), designed for Depot Operators.
4.  **`components/Dashboard.tsx`**: Updated to include a "View Switcher" (Into-Plane vs. Depot) specifically for System Admins and Executives.
5.  **`components/Schedule.tsx`**: Updated the modal input styles to ensure high contrast (dark text on white background) for readability.
6.  **`App.tsx`**: Registered the new routes (`admin`, `reports`, `seaplane`).
7.  **`components/Sidebar.tsx`**: Updated the navigation menu to expose these new modules to the appropriate user roles.

Building a mission-critical aviation fuel management system is a complex undertaking, especially when balancing strict international safety standards with the unpredictable nature of apron network connectivity. To ensure this system is robust, secure, and future-proofed for modern airport operations, it must be built on an Offline-First, Cloud-Native architecture.

Here is the recommended System Architecture and Tech Stack to hand over to your lead developer or engineering team.

1. Architectural Paradigm: Offline-First Edge Client
Because your Into-Plane (ITP) operators will frequently encounter dead zones on the tarmac, the mobile application cannot simply be "offline-capable"—it must be "offline-first."

This means the application reads and writes exclusively to a local database on the tablet first. A background synchronization engine then continuously monitors the network state. When the connection is restored, it pushes the cached data (meter readings, timestamps, QC checks) to the central server and pulls the latest AOCC flight schedules.

2. Recommended Tech Stack
Frontend: Mobile & Tablet (Apron Operations)
Framework: React Native. This allows you to build a high-performance native app for both iOS and Android from a single codebase, making hardware procurement for the apron much more flexible.

Local Database & Sync: WatermelonDB or PowerSync (with SQLite). These are state-of-the-art tools specifically designed for offline-first React Native applications. They handle relational data effortlessly and manage the complex sync queues and conflict resolutions required when an operator reconnects to the network.

State Management: Zustand or Redux Toolkit.

Frontend: Web Portal (Depot, Managers & Executives)
Framework: Next.js (React). A highly structured, scalable framework perfect for building the complex, data-heavy interfaces required for the Executive Dashboards, Depot static tank logs, and advanced Jet A-1 forecasting models.

Data Visualization: Apache ECharts or Chart.js. These libraries are excellent for rendering the required donut charts for tank capacities, heat maps for peak utilization, and scatter graphs for refueling durations.

Backend (The Core Engine)
Framework: NestJS (Node.js + TypeScript). NestJS enforces a strict, modular enterprise architecture. Using TypeScript across both the frontend and backend ensures data consistency (e.g., ensuring a timestamp is always treated as a timestamp) and reduces bugs.

Alternative: FastAPI (Python). If your team has stronger Python expertise, FastAPI is incredibly fast and highly suited for building the complex calculation engines required for your 3-scenario forecasting model.

Database Architecture
Primary Database: PostgreSQL. The relationships between flight schedules, totalizer meter runs, storage facilities, and granular timestamps are highly relational. PostgreSQL is the gold standard for enterprise data integrity.

Caching Layer: Redis. To ensure the dashboards load instantly, Redis should cache frequently accessed, heavy queries (like the 5-year historical data overlays or the daily stock summary).

3. Integration & API Layer
To ensure seamless communication with external airport systems without compromising your internal data:

API Protocol: GraphQL or RESTful APIs.

AOCC & SITA AMS Integration: Implement a dedicated microservice or message broker (like RabbitMQ) to ingest live flight data from the AOCC and handle the conditional pull of "Route" data from SITA AMS for profitability analysis. This keeps external data streams decoupled from your core database.

4. Security & RBAC Implementation
Strict data boundaries are foundational to this system, as the Fuel Services Section must retain exclusive operational control.

Authentication: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (via providers like Auth0 or Microsoft Entra ID if integrating with your existing corporate directory).

Authorization: Implement strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) via JSON Web Tokens (JWT). The backend routes must be explicitly guarded by role claims:

Admin: Global technical access.

Manager: Read/write dashboard access.

Operator (ITP/Depot): Restrict to POST/PUT endpoints for data input only, with hard blocks on editing past records.

Executive/Commercial: Strictly scoped to GET endpoints for aggregated analytics, blocking access to technical stock tables.

Task: Transform the "SkyFuel FMS" into a world-class, modern Enterprise SaaS application. The goal is to move away from generic Tailwind layouts and toward a "Linear-style" or "Apple-inspired" aesthetic that prioritizes high-density data clarity and premium UI/UX.

1. Visual Design & Branding
Glassmorphism & Depth: Replace flat white backgrounds with subtle glassmorphism (backdrop-blur-md) and layered elevations. Use thin, high-contrast borders (border-slate-200/50) instead of heavy shadows.

Typography: Implement a dynamic type scale using an interface-focused font like Inter or Geist. Headers should be tighter, and data points should use tabular-nums for alignment.

Refined Color Palette: Stick to the aviation blue but introduce a "Dark Mode" foundation. Use semantic colors for fuel types (e.g., Jet-A1 as a deep indigo, Diesel as a forest green).

2. Architectural Improvements (App.tsx & State)
State Management: Transition from basic useState for tanks to a more robust pattern (like a Redux-style reducer or TanStack Query) to handle "Optimistic Updates" for the offline mode.

Framer Motion: Integrate framer-motion for page transitions. Views should not just "appear"; they should slide or fade smoothly to give the app a native feel.

Command Palette: Add a CMD+K interface for quick navigation between "IntoPlane" and "Stock" modules, essential for power users.

3. Functional Module Upgrades
Dashboard: Replace basic stats with "Skeleton Loaders" and sparkline charts. The "Offline Indicator" should be a subtle pulsing ring around the user's avatar.

Interactive Tanks: In the Stock and Bridging views, create visual SVG tank indicators that "fill" based on the currentLevel vs capacity percentage.

Real-time Activity Feed: Add a "Live Ledger" on the sidebar or a slide-over panel showing a stream of fuel movements as they happen.

4. UX Enhancements
Contextual Role UI: Instead of just a dropdown, create a "User Persona" onboarding or a more elegant profile switcher that updates the entire theme of the app based on the role (e.g., Operator mode gets larger touch targets).

Micro-feedback: Add "Toast" notifications for successful tank updates and "Haptic-like" visual feedback when buttons are clicked.

5. Code Quality
Component Logic: Abstract the "View Router" in App.tsx into a separate Layout component.

Strict Typing: Ensure all events (like the Role Switcher) are fully typed and move MOCK_DATA into a dedicated /services layer to simulate API fetching with latencies.

Please provide the updated App.tsx, a refined index.css with modern CSS variables, and an example of the modernized Dashboard.tsx component.

Key Improvements Suggested
1. The "Glass" Sidebar
Instead of a solid slate sidebar, the modern approach uses a semi-transparent blur.

Old: bg-slate-900

New: bg-white/70 backdrop-blur-xl border-r border-slate-200/50

2. Tabular Numbers for Data
In aviation, numbers are everything. In your constants.ts or CSS, ensure fuel volumes use:
font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
This prevents the layout from "jumping" when numbers change (like a clock or a fuel meter).

3. Smart Redirects 2.0
In your handleRoleSwitch in App.tsx, instead of just changing the view, add a "Loading" state. Modern apps "prepare" the workspace, which gives the user a sense of the app doing heavy lifting.

4. Interactive Tank Visualization
Instead of showing 3,200,000 / 5,000,000, use a CSS custom property to drive a fill animation:
